text:
Jaden Schwartz is 34, on his third NHL team, and doing exactly what Colorado brought him in to do: play 13.7 minutes a night on a deep forward group and chip in. Seven goals and 14 points in 24 games is a pace above anything his chances suggest, though. He has scored on 17% of his shots against 13% last season, and those 7 goals come from 4.0 expected (the quality of his chances, in goals). The Avalanche have also scored 4.1 more goals than expected with him on the ice.

The slowdown has already started. Since a two-goal night in Chicago on Nov. 2 he has one goal in nine games, with only 1.7 expected goals across his last ten. That's not a slump so much as the number settling.

What's real is the transition game. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 54% of his shots coming off the rush last season and 67% of his exits leaving the zone with the puck. On a team this fast, that's a useful middle-six piece, and a Stanley Cup winner from 2019 who knows the role.
headline: Schwartz's goals came early, and they came hot
